grass-a#0.notes: two summits on a long ridge, slopes in the meadow's own green: melts into the grass ground

grass-a#1.notes: a heap of soft lumps, reads as a pile of hillocks rather than one massif

grass-a#2.notes: high green mountain with a grey rocky crown and long spurs; lower slopes match the meadow

grass-a#3.notes: twin summits with deep shaded gullies, a clear ridge silhouette

steppe-a#0.notes: straight cut bottom edge and a stray white line under it: a boxy plate

steppe-a#1.notes: flat cut bottom with a white line, the sides end in vertical walls

steppe-a#2.notes: jagged triple summit with long spurs tapering into the plain

steppe-a#3.notes: terraced cake mesa with separate rocks beside it

badlands-a#0.notes: two flat-topped buttes on one long strata ridge over a red scree skirt

badlands-a#1.notes: one broad table butte with fluted strata and a wide scree foot

badlands-a#2.notes: tall butte joined to a lower table, scree skirt in the plain's red

badlands-a#3.notes: two boxy stacks side by side with rubble: reads as separate blocks

snow-a#0.notes: the lower snow is a rectangular plate with straight sides

snow-a#1.notes: three snowy summits with rock ribs, slopes taper at both sides

snow-a#2.notes: one big pointed alpine mountain with long snowy spurs

snow-a#3.notes: rectangular snow plate under the peaks, boxy base

sand-a#0.notes: long fluted sandstone ridge with two mesas on its crest

sand-a#1.notes: tall spires on a broad base, the foot spreads into sand

sand-a#2.notes: wind-carved butte joined to a lower table rock

sand-a#3.notes: three striped pyramids side by side: reads as built, not a massif

grass-b#0.notes: long low ridge of three summits, slopes taper into the meadow at both sides

grass-b#1.notes: broad massif with a rocky top and a lower shoulder, meadow-green foot

grass-b#2.notes: wide mountain with a short grey rocky crest, long tapering slopes

grass-b#3.notes: twin sharp summits with deep gullies; a darker green that still sits on the meadow

steppe-b#0.notes: two rock summits whose straw-grass foot spreads into the plain

steppe-b#1.notes: high jagged summit with long spurs, no line under the foot

steppe-b#2.notes: big craggy mountain over a wide straw-coloured foot

steppe-b#3.notes: three points with deep gullies, the foot melts into the plain

badlands-b#0.notes: long flat-topped mesa of fluted cliffs over a red scree skirt

badlands-b#1.notes: notched mesa with level strata, a wide scree foot

badlands-b#2.notes: butte joined to a long sloping ridge: one big form

badlands-b#3.notes: stepped boxy blocks: reads as a terraced cake

snow-b#0.notes: twin snowy summits whose snow foot spreads into the snowfield

snow-b#1.notes: lower slopes bare dark rock: a grey block sitting on the snow

snow-b#2.notes: three peaks with snowfields between them, tapering at both sides

snow-b#3.notes: row of snowy points over a broad snow foot that melts into the ground

sand-b#0.notes: flat cut bottom with a white line under it

sand-b#1.notes: flat cut bottom with a white line; the knobs read as a pair of buns

sand-b#2.notes: two boxy towers on a flat cut base with a white line

sand-b#3.notes: rock arch (rejected subject) on a flat cut base with a white line

sand-c#0.notes: low ridge of two rounded wind-carved knobs over a sand foot

sand-c#1.notes: tall spire on a shoulder, the sand foot tapers into the dunes

sand-c#2.notes: one broad mesa with fluted cliffs on a wide drifted-sand skirt

sand-c#3.notes: craggy twin summit with strata, the foot spreads into sand

wasteland-a#0.notes: low jagged basalt ridge with ember cracks over an ash foot

wasteland-a#1.notes: three broken points with deep gullies, ash-grey foot melts into the plain

wasteland-a#2.notes: big craggy basalt mountain with long spurs, faint ember cracks

wasteland-a#3.notes: high sharp summit with shoulders, tapering ash slopes

jungle-a#0.notes: two limestone towers joined by a mossy ridge over a jungle-green foot

jungle-a#1.notes: three rounded limestone towers under moss, one broad form

jungle-a#2.notes: steep green mountain with grey limestone cliffs and a mossy foot

jungle-a#3.notes: busy hanging vines and loose rocks at the foot: reads as rubble

frosting-a#0.notes: a strawberry cake on a plate: two berries on an icing layer with a white line under the foot

frosting-a#1.notes: boxy rock-candy cubes in a row with stray thin lines down both sides; reads as blocks, not one mountain

frosting-a#2.notes: a big gumdrop mountain under a dripping icing crown; its wide pale pink skirt is the frosting's own colour and melts into the icing plain

frosting-a#3.notes: three gumdrop summits joined by poured icing over a frosting-pink foot that vanishes into the plain

swamp-a#0.notes: two mossy peat summits on long mud-coloured slopes that spread out and sink into the swamp ground

swamp-a#1.notes: a craggy peat massif with mossy ledges and hanging moss over a mud foot; distinct from the rounded ones

swamp-a#2.notes: one moss-capped dome over a dark stump base: reads as a giant mossy stump or mushroom, not a massif

swamp-a#3.notes: three mossy rock summits with deep gullies running down into mud-coloured slopes

volcanic-a#0.notes: three sharp basalt summits on long dark cinder slopes that melt into the volcanic plain (the wasteland massifs stood on a pale ash rim)

volcanic-a#1.notes: a broken volcanic cone seen from the front, its rim only a low ellipse, one ember crack, dark cinder foot (a front-view cone, not a crater seen from above)

volcanic-a#2.notes: a jagged multi-summit basalt ridge with glowing ember cracks over a cinder foot: the clearest volcanic form

volcanic-a#3.notes: twin broken summits on a broad cone with fluted cinder slopes; the dark foot sits in the ground

frosting-b#0.notes: twin gumdrop summits under one dripping icing cap on a wide frosting skirt that melts into the plain

frosting-b#1.notes: a big gumdrop mountain with a lower iced shoulder; the pale pink foot vanishes into the frosting

frosting-b#2.notes: three iced gumdrop summits joined on one frosting skirt, a candy range in one form

frosting-b#3.notes: two loose gumdrop lumps beside the dome read as separate candies, not one massif

swamp-b#0.notes: a long low mossy ridge with two rounded summits; mud-coloured slopes spread out into the swamp

swamp-b#1.notes: stacked square peat boulders read as built blocks, not a mountain face

swamp-b#2.notes: three mossy knobs over fluted peat slopes running down into mud

swamp-b#3.notes: craggy peat summits over long mossy slopes tapering to points; the boldest swamp silhouette
